questions.problem: Find all of the real solutions to the equation $3{w}^{3}-4{w}^{2}+12w-16=0.$
questions.worked_solution:
We proceed to factor the left-hand side by grouping:

$$
\begin{aligned}3{w}^{3}-4{w}^{2}+12w-16 & = \\ (3{w}^{3}-4{w}^{2})+(12w-16) & = \\ {w}^{2}(3w-4)+4(3w-4) & = \\ (3w-4)\cdot {w}^{2}+(3w-4)\cdot 4 & = \\ (3w-4)({w}^{2}+4) & \end{aligned}
$$

Then, we solve $(3w-4)({w}^{2}+4)=0$ by setting each factor equal to $0.$

- Setting the factor $(3w-4)$ equal to $0,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}3w-4 & =0 \\ 3w & =4 \\ w & =\frac{4}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

- Setting the factor $({w}^{2}+4)$ equal to $0,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{w}^{2}+4 & =0 \\ {w}^{2} & =-4.\end{aligned}
$$

Since a squared real number cannot be negative, the equation ${w}^{2}+4=0$ has no real solutions.

Therefore,  $w=\frac{4}{3}$ is the only real solution.

questions.worked_solution:
First, we rewrite $\frac{1}{100\,000}$ as a power of $10$ (the base of the common logarithm) as follows:

$$
\frac{1}{100\,000}=\frac{1}{{10}^{5}}={10}^{-5}
$$

Therefore, we have:

$$
\operatorname{log}⁡(\frac{1}{100\,000})=\operatorname{log}⁡({10}^{-5})
$$

The common logarithm reverses the action of the exponent. The principle is:

$$
\operatorname{log}⁡({10}^{x})=x
$$

In our case, we have $x=-5.$ Therefore:

$$
\operatorname{log}⁡({10}^{-5})=-5
$$

questions.problem: Is the function $f(x)=\sqrt{20+x}$, where $x\in [-20,+\infty )$, even, odd, or neither?
questions.worked_solution:
Recall that

- a function is even if $f(-x)=f(x)$ for all $x$

- a function is odd if $f(-x)=-f(x)$ for all $x$

Computing $f(-x)$ for the given function and comparing it to $f(x),$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}f(-x) & =\sqrt{20+(-x)} \\  & =\sqrt{20-x}\end{aligned}
$$

Since $f(-x)\ne f(x),$ the function is not even. 

Lastly, we compute $-f(x)$ and get

$$
\begin{aligned}-f(x) & =-[\sqrt{20+x}\,] \\  & =-\sqrt{20+x}\end{aligned}
$$

Since $f(-x)\ne -f(x)$, the function is not odd. 

Therefore, the function is neither even nor odd.

questions.worked_solution:
The roots of $f(z)$ are the solutions to the equation $f(z)=0.$ In our case, we have

$$
\frac{{z}^{2}+3z+2}{{z}^{2}+z}=0.
$$

First, we factor the numerator and denominator and cancel any common factors, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(z) & =\frac{{z}^{2}+3z+2}{{z}^{2}+z} \\  & =\frac{(z+2)(z+1)}{z(z+1)} \\  & =\frac{(z+2)\cancel{(z+1)}}{z\cancel{(z+1)}} \\  & =\frac{z+2}{z}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we set the numerator equal to zero and solve for $z:$

$$
\begin{aligned}z+2 & =0\,⟹\,z=-2\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution to $f(z)=0$ is $z=-2.$

questions.problem: Find the formula for the $n$th term of an arithmetic sequence if the first term is $-11$ and the common difference is $3.$
questions.worked_solution:
The formula for the $n$th term of an arithmetic sequence (in function notation) is

$$
f(n)=f(1)+(n-1)d.
$$

We are told that the first term is $f(1)=-11$ and the common difference is $d=3.$ So, we substitute into the formula and simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(n) & =f(1)+(n-1)d \\  & =-11+(n-1)(3) \\  & =-11+3n-3 \\  & =3n-14\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the formula for the $n$th term is $f(n)=3n-14.$

$$
